title: pvWavefrontOBJReader
body:
## pvWavefrontOBJReader

Reads Wavefront .obj geometry into polydata with polygons and lines, keeping normals and texture coordinates when the file provides them. Materials (.mtl) are not applied to the data. Use it for surface models exported by modelling or CAD tools; use readSTL for STL and pvglTFReader for glTF scenes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- OBJ has no unit convention; check whether coordinates are millimetres or metres before combining with simulation data.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

Native constructor: `WavefrontOBJReader`. Identity: `sources/objreader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FileName` | This property specifies the file name for the OBJ reader. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvWavefrontOBJReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
